newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Solzhenitsyn leaves hospital after heart problem.
newsitem.headline: Solzhenitsyn leaves hospital after heart problem.

text.p: Writer Alexander Solzhenitsyn, a relentless critic of both Soviet and Russian leaders, has left hospital where he spent two weeks with a heart condition, Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.
The agency, quoting Solzhenitsyn's wife Natalia, did not say when the writer was discharged from the hospital but said he was in a "stable condition" and planned a gradual return to work.
The 79-year-old Nobel Prize winner had been admitted to the Central Clinical Hospital on May 12 with heart problems.
Solzhenitsyn won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1970 for writings which publicised the harshness of the Soviet prison camp system.
Expelled from the Soviet Union in 1974, he lived in exile in rural America for 20 years before returning to Russia where he blasted its new leaders for being just as bad as the communists.
Solzhenitzyn, who wrote "A day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich", "First Circle" and "Cancer Ward", dropped from public view after his weekly television programme was taken off the air in 1995.
The bearded firebrand, who says Russia has lost its spiritual roots and favours a kind of 19th century rural nationalism, was criticised for being out of touch.
